summary: MaterialDNA schema-v2 maintenance.repairCount accepts any finite non-negative numeric value whose floor equals itself, with no safe-integer upper bound. Canonical recipe values above 2^53-1 are therefore not injectively representable as Lua numbers: distinct conceptual repair counts can collapse before validation/canonical sealing. This is inconsistent with the contract's bounded canonical numeric domain and should fail closed at the exact IEEE-754 safe-integer boundary.
evidence: src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau validateNonNegativeInteger checks finite, >= 0, and math.floor(value) == value but has no maximum; its only caller is maintenance.repairCount.
MaterialDNA recipeVersion is already bounded to a deterministic integer domain, while repairCount remains unbounded despite being canonical recipe content included in revision seals.
Docs/MATERIAL_DNA_CONTRACT.md states numeric plausibility ranges are finite and bounded and canonical material truth must not silently alias.
A source-only regression can accept 9007199254740991 and reject 9007199254740992 without changing existing fixtures or Studio behavior.

metadata.recommendedFix: bound maintenance.repairCount to [0, 9007199254740991] with exact boundary regression
